lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: central idea emergence and refinement

studentTask.text: Today's focus: central idea emergence and refinement. Essential question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to central idea emergence and refinement change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim? By the end of this lesson you should be able to: Explain what central idea emergence and refinement means and name the textual signal that tells you it is in play. You'll need: course notebook or digital equivalent; the unit's assigned texts, in an accessible reading representation; citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course.

guidedSupport.text:
Work through this with a facilitator, tutor, or on your own if you're ready:
- Welcome and retrieval: Open with a short retrieval prompt on today's lesson. Ask the learner to predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.
- Ungraded diagnostic: Ask the learner to attempt today's lesson cold, before any instruction. Record what they already do well. Nothing here is scored, and errors here are data, not failure.
- Surface and name: Name what the diagnostic revealed in neutral, non-character language. State the unit question and what will count as evidence by the end of it.
- Orientation to the unit: Walk the unit's destination: Write a formal explanatory article with headings and one graphic that genuinely clarifies a complex idea.. The learner writes down what they think will be hardest about it and why. The tutor may question this prediction but may not write it.
- Goal setting: The learner records one specific thing about today's lesson they intend to be able to do by the end of the unit.

If you get stuck:
- If prerequisite gap: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for today's lesson, re-teach it on a short passage, then retry one fresh item. Do not write the learner's response.
- If repeated error pattern: Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of today's lesson.
- If procedure without understanding: Ask the learner to explain why the move for today's lesson works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.

independentEvidenceTask.text: Attempt today's lesson without instruction, then record a personal goal for the unit. When finished: Name one thing about today's lesson you can already do and one you cannot do yet.
